findings.title: HTTP probe timeout is per-socket-op, not a total deadline; check can block far past timeout_seconds
findings.evidence: response = http_get(url, timeout=timeout) with no stream/max-redirect control; requests applies the float to each connect/read, follows up to 30 redirects by default, and reads the body fully because stream is not set.
findings.recommendation: Bound the whole probe: pass allow_redirects with a bounded count (or False), set stream=True and close/max-read the body, and enforce a hard wall-clock deadline via a separate connect/read tuple or an outer Future.result(timeout=...) so a redirect chain or slow-drip dependency cannot hold the /healthz handler open.

findings.title: Health path raises ValueError/TypeError on bad timeout instead of reporting down
findings.evidence: if timeout_seconds <= 0: raise ValueError(...) contradicts _run_probe's stated principle that a health check must never raise; a misconfigured env timeout of 0 or a non-numeric value turns /healthz into a 500 (TypeError on the comparison) rather than a 503/down payload.
findings.recommendation: Coerce to float inside a try and treat invalid/zero timeouts as a reported failure (e.g. status down with error ConfigurationError) instead of raising out of healthcheck.

findings.title: Probes run serially with no aggregate deadline; worst case is N times the timeout
findings.evidence: checks are built one probe after another, each allowed the full timeout_seconds, so N registered probes can hold the endpoint for up to N*timeout_seconds (2s * N) and trip LB timeouts that then look like an outage.
findings.recommendation: Either run probes concurrently with an overall deadline (ThreadPoolExecutor + as_completed with a total budget) or document timeout_seconds as a per-probe budget and expose a separate total budget.

findings.title: Probes are invoked as probe(timeout=...) but that call contract is undocumented and mis-wiring is silent
findings.evidence: probe(timeout=timeout_seconds) requires the callback to accept a keyword named exactly timeout; a probe wired as def probe(t) raises TypeError which _run_probe converts to status down, so a wiring bug is reported as a dependency outage (and a core-named one drains the instance).
findings.recommendation: Document the probe protocol explicitly (a Protocol/typing alias) and/or invoke positionally while validating callables at registration; consider distinguishing TypeError/AttributeError from dependency exceptions in the payload.

findings.title: Core status depends on hard-coded probe names with no validation that a core probe is registered
findings.evidence: core_down is derived solely from membership of the probe name in CORE_PROBES, so a database probe registered as db/pg/postgres, or an empty probes mapping, yields 200 ok/degraded and the instance is never drained.
findings.recommendation: Validate at startup/healthcheck that at least one core probe is present (and reject unknown/misnamed core probes), or make criticality an explicit per-probe attribute rather than a name string.

findings.title: TCP probe timeout applies per resolved address, so total connect time can exceed the timeout
findings.evidence: socket.create_connection loops over getaddrinfo results applying timeout to each attempt and DNS resolution itself is unbounded, so a dual-stack host with one blackholed family can take ~2x timeout_seconds or more.
findings.recommendation: Resolve once, attempt addresses under a shared deadline (or rely on an outer hard timeout per probe) and document that timeout_seconds bounds the whole probe.

findings.title: Docstring promises 2xx but raise_for_status also accepts 3xx
findings.evidence: response.raise_for_status() only raises for 4xx/5xx, so a final 3xx (e.g. 304, or a redirect without Location) is reported ok despite the docstring saying success means a 2xx response.
findings.recommendation: Assert response.ok and 200 <= status_code < 300 explicitly, or relax the docstring to say any non-error response.

findings.title: No tests for the 503 vs 200 vs degraded mapping
findings.evidence: healthcheck is the whole decision surface of the endpoint (core_down -> 503, any_down -> degraded/200, all ok) and this change ships with no test file or test command exercised.
findings.recommendation: Add tests with injected probes covering: core probe down -> 503, non-core down -> 200 degraded, all ok -> 200, probe raising -> down with error type, timeout<=0 rejected, and empty probes mapping.
